summary: A windswept point on Conanicut Island lit since 1749, the third lighthouse in America and a proving ground for fog signals; the granite tower dates from 1856.

access.note: Grounds in Beavertail State Park; museum in the keeper's quarters opens seasonally; the 2024 transfer release says visitors may climb the tower.

notes_for_editor: Rich station but no annual reports before 1891 are in the corpus and Chronicling America gave nothing useful for Beavertail; the keeper chapter leans on the USLHS roster and New England Lighthouses (a secondary, copyrighted source used in our own words, with short quotations of older reports as it prints them). Disagreements stated in the text: size of the 1749 tower (58 ft NRHP and marker, 68 ft LighthouseFriends); date of the stone tower (1753 marker, 1754 JHS papers, 1755 NRHP); whether the circular foundation is the 1749 or the 1755 tower (NRHP vs markers); date of the first Daboll trumpet (1851 NRHP, 1856 Johnson); steam/hot-air engine dates (marker 1857, Bulletin 1868); siren date (LHB 10 Nov 1899, Bulletin 1900); tower paint (LHB Aug 1899, NRHP 1900); tower height (52 ft LF, 64 or 68 ft Reed release, 64 ft light height USLHS); Manders's start (marker 1913, USLHS assistant 1914 and head 1918); 1815 hurricane damage (NEL vs LF). The Beavertail marker spells the Weedens 'Wheeler' and 'Damaris'. Lighthouse Service Bulletin 1939 OCR is column-interleaved, so quotes from it are short fragments; its pages are matched to PDF pages 20-23 by grep. LHB 1894 and 1899/1900 are cited by scan page (printed page not confirmed except 1894 p. 306). Johnson 1889 Whale Rock distance reads '1|' in the OCR, probably 1.5 miles. The 1938 school-bus deaths rest on the museum marker and the Jamestown Press; LighthouseFriends's longer account (including a driver's remarks and a later death) was not used because it has no checkable primary source here. The USLHS roster lines were matched to 'person' slugs by the roster tool. Post-1960 keepers and Coast Guard names appear only in the roster as the archive prints them. 'Today' relies on the June 2024 Senate release for the tower being open to climb; hours were not verified (museum site blocked). Fact-check 2026-10-22: the Bonnet Point audibility quotation is on printed p. 307 of the 1894 report (footnote now says pp. 306-307); Johnson's Whale Rock distance reads '1|' in the OCR and his earlier paragraph says 'less than a mile and a half', so 'about 1.5 miles'. Carpender's remark and the LighthouseFriends 1754 date were added for balance.
